html:
On 6 July 1917, fighters of the Arab Revolt took the port of Aqaba on the Red Sea from the Ottomans, after a long march across the desert. The British officer T. E. Lawrence rode with them.

The Ottoman guns at Aqaba pointed out to sea. The Arab force, led by Auda abu Tayi of the Howeitat tribe and Sharif Nasir, came at it from the land side, and the garrison surrendered.

Aqaba became the base from which the Arab army under Prince Faisal moved north, beside the British, to Damascus in 1918. It is the scene of the film Lawrence of Arabia. The Revolt led to the Emirate of Transjordan. See also Ottoman Empire.
